formulas.formula: Every flip, every fee, every dollar of profit.
1. Platforms: check the fee % and fixed fee for each place you sell. They estimate your fees when you leave Fees blank.
2. Inventory: add each item when you buy it (cost, date, where you found it). Add the listing date, price and platform when you list it.
3. When it sells, type the sold date and sale price (plus shipping, and the real fees if you know them).
4. Expenses: supplies, mileage, apps and other costs that aren't tied to one item.
5. Monthly Summary, Platforms, Sources & Categories, Aging and Dashboard update on their own.
Sale price + shipping the buyer paid − fees − shipping you paid − other costs − what you paid for it.
Profit ÷ what you paid. 300% means you made three times your money back.
Leave Fees blank to estimate them from Platforms. Type the real number from your sale to override.
Items sitting more than 90 days get a nudge to drop the price or relist.
Clear the white cells on Inventory and Expenses (sample rows), then add your own.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Yellow: listed and waiting, or getting old.
Red: a loss, something stale, or an entry to check.
Thank you for your purchase! Happy flipping.

section_bars.label: REVENUE AND NET PROFIT BY MONTH

formulas.formula: ="Your reselling year at a glance, as of "&TEXT('Inventory'!$AD$5,"mmmm d, yyyy")&"."
One row per item. Type the white columns as the item moves from bought to listed to sold.
Business costs that aren't tied to one item: supplies, mileage, apps, storage, equipment.
Month by month for the year on Inventory. Item profit is from items sold that month; net profit also takes off your expenses.
Fee % and fixed fee per sale for each platform (check yours: platforms change fees). Results are for items sold in the year on Inventory.
Where your best flips come from, and what sells best. Bought = items bought this year; sold numbers are items sold this year. Type your sources and categories in column B (they become dropdowns).
Everything not sold yet, oldest first. Days count from the date you bought it.
